name: North Ridge
overview: Half Moon is a crescent-shaped granite fin on the north half of Kangaroo Ridge, between Wallaby Peak and Big Kangaroo, about two miles east of the North Cascades Highway at Washington Pass. It has no easy way up: every line to its summit is a roped rock climb, and the easiest is fifth class. The North Ridge starts in the deep notch just north of the fin and climbs about seven pitches on or just west of the crest to the summit. The rock is friable and eroded on the first pitch or two and much better above, and the upper ridge has real exposure over the west face. Fred and Helmy Beckey and Walt Varney made the first ascent of the peak on June 17, 1942. The route sees few parties, so expect lichen, some loose rock and anchors that may need rebuilding.
beta: Start in the deep notch north of the peak and climb the broad buttress above it toward the ridge crest. The first pitch has hollow, friable rock that improves steadily on the second. From there the line stays on the crest or just west of it, belaying at ledges, with steeper crack climbing in the middle of the route. High on the ridge a pitch traverses the west side of the narrowing crest with big exposure over the west face before working back to the crest. The last pitch is easy climbing on the crest, then a short scramble to the summit. Seven pitches is the usual count; belay at the obvious ledges rather than running pitches together, which causes rope drag.
descent_text: Descend the route. From the summit, downclimb the easy but exposed top of the ridge to the first anchor and rappel back down the line of ascent, using the ledges on the crest and its west side as stations, until you are back in the notch north of the peak. Carry two ropes; the stations are a mix of old fixed pitons, bolts, slung horns and nuts, some parties have found no fixed anchors at all, and any tat left there should be inspected and backed up. From the notch, descend the loose scree gully carefully (keep the party close to limit rockfall), and at its foot rejoin the climbers' path and follow it back north to the hairpin pullout on the highway.
descent: Rappel the North Ridge back to the notch north of the peak, then descend the scree gully and reverse the approach to the highway.
rappels: The route is descended by rappelling the line of ascent back to the notch. Carry two ropes. Anchors are a mix of fixed pitons, bolts, slung horns and nuts of varying age, and some parties have found none at all, so bring slings and cord to back up or build each station.

pitch_detail.notes: From the notch, climb the broad buttress toward the ridge crest. The rock on the first pitch is hollow and eroded; it improves markedly on the second.
Continue on or just west of the crest on better rock, belaying at the obvious ledges; stopping at ledges rather than running pitches together avoids rope drag.
Where the ridge narrows, climb on the west side of the crest with big exposure over the west face, then work back to the crest.
A few exposed moves on the crest lead to an easy scramble to the summit.

fa: Helmy Beckey, Fred Beckey, and Walt Varney, June 17, 1942 (first ascent of the peak)
